title: Temporal soft-merge: tenant-aware compaction and decode-window pacing for paged KV
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Background:
Paged attention workloads show long-tail decode stalls and high fragmentation in the KV page pool under mixed tenant traffic. LRU-style evict-on-demand causes frequent micro-thrashing: hot tenants keep reloading small fragments, while cold fragments linger and prevent contiguous free regions needed for efficient prefill and kernel coplacement.

Goal:
Reduce fragmentation and tail decode latency without increasing average token cost. Provide a safe incremental rollout path and tenant-aware fairness so high-throughput customers retain expected SLOs while low-touch tenants don't induce excessive compaction overhead.

Proposal summary:
1) Temporal soft-merge (TSM): instead of immediately reclaiming small, scattered free fragments, mark them as tombstoned and make them eligible for background soft-merge compaction. The soft-merge process scans adjacent tombstoned/friction fragments and coalesces them into contiguous superframes when a low-CPU window is detected. This reduces future allocation scatter and improves kernel coplacement success rate.

2) Tenant-aware scoring: fragments gain or lose compaction priority based on tenant touch-frequency, recent decode-window latency contribution, and estimated reclaim benefit (contiguity created). A small per-tenant quota prevents noisy tenants from consuming compaction cycles.

3) Decode-window pacing admission: apply an adaptive microbatch pacing layer for prefill/decode admission that limits concurrent decodes per-shard based on current KV fragmentation metrics and recent decode 99th percentile. This prevents escalations where many small decodes trigger simultaneous prefills that fragment the pool.

Design details:
- Tombstone lifecycle: Tombstoned fragments carry a tombstone timestamp and a decay score; only fragments older than tombstone_grace (configurable, default 60s) are considered for soft-merge. Immediate reads still see tombstoned entries (no data loss).
- Soft-merge worker: background worker runs prioritized compaction rounds when host GPU/CPU load < threshold and memory pressure indicates benefit. Merges are opportunistic and abortable (preempted by higher-priority infra ops).
- Admission controller: maintains shard-level token bucket whose refill rate is tuned by fragmentation ratio and 99th decode latency. If the bucket is exhausted, prefill requests are queued with backoff and instrumented metrics.
- Data structures: use a lightweight fragment-run table per-shard with run-length encoding of free/allocated runs to keep compaction bookkeeping O(number_of_runs) where runs << pages.

Metrics and success criteria:
- 99th percentile decode latency decrease >= 15% on multi-tenant synthetic burst workload (target).
- Fragmentation ratio (free runs per free pages) reduced >= 40% after compaction under steady state.
- No regression in average tokens/sec cost (<= 5% increase allowed during canary).
- Compaction worker CPU/GPU overhead < 2% of node resources on average.

Testing plan:
- Microbench: deterministic workload replay with tenant mix (10 tenants, 1 hot, 9 medium/cold) to measure fragmentation and decode tail.
- Staging canary: feature-flagged rollout to a small dedicated cluster with traffic shaping to mirror production.
- Chaos test: simulate node pressure and prefill storms to ensure admission controller queues and backoff avoid SLO violation.

Rollout plan:
- Dev / bench cycle (2 weeks): implement TSM + admission controller with unit tests and bench harness.
- Canary 1 (1% of traffic, runtime-1.21): monitor metrics, kill switch ready.
- Canary 2 (10%): tune tombstone_grace and admission token rates.
- Gradual ramp to 100% with feature off-path fallback to LRU eviction and immediate disable if customer_impact > high.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Dashboards: paged-kv/fragmentation, decode-latency/percentiles, compactor/cpu-util, admission/queue-depth.
- Alerts: decode-99th > baseline*1.5 for >5m, compaction-error-rate > 0.5% per hour, admission-queue-depth > 500 requests.

Migration & Compatibility:
- Backwards compatible: tombstoning is purely an allocation layer change; on-disk model formats unchanged.
- Rollback: disable compactor and set admission controller to permissive mode to resume old behavior.

- Benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/runtime/paged-kv/tsm-bench
